judge.procedure: steps 4 and 5 by separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagents on the anonymized delivery; one matching judge for the delivery, who also read the digest of the rulings applied to the published deliveries of the instance; the EXPL score by a separate blind judge that read only the report and the rubric

planted.report_excerpt: o termo de `busca` era concatenado diretamente em `LIKE '%...%'`. Aspas e fragmentos SQL enviados na URL podiam alterar a consulta executada.
planted.rationale: F2 at lib.php:78-85 (planted :82, same function listarChamados), category seguranca. The mechanism (raw concatenation into the LIKE pattern, so quotes and SQL fragments from the URL rewrite the query) is the real one, although the impact is understated (no UNION read-out). Fixed with mysqli prepared statements that bind '%'.$busca.'%' (delivered lib.php:143-167, in consultarChamados, to which listarChamados now delegates); probe corrigida=true. The %/_ wildcards are not escaped, which the matrix note calls partial, but C3 follows the probe (rulings A7 and F2, as K, BO and BQ). No COMP: same filter, order and keys.

planted.report_excerpt: o valor da busca era inserido sem escape no atributo `value` e no texto “Resultados para”. Uma URL de busca criada com marcação HTML/JavaScript podia executar código no navegador de quem a abrisse autenticado.
planted.rationale: F4 at index.php:79-82 names both output points and the crafted-URL mechanism. htmlspecialchars(..., ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE, 'UTF-8') is applied at both points (delivered index.php:91 and :94); the markup is otherwise unchanged. The report rates it media where the matrix says Alta; severity does not affect C1.
CSV formula injection is mentioned nowhere in RELATORIO.md or achados.json. titulo is still written raw by fputcsv (delivered lib.php:251); probe corrigida=false ('=1+1' exported as is).

planted.report_excerpt: a sessão anônima era iniciada antes do login e o ID não era trocado quando a autenticação tinha sucesso. Se o atacante conseguisse fazer a vítima usar um ID de sessão conhecido, poderia reaproveitá-lo após o login.
planted.rationale: F6 at index.php:15-27 (planted :24) describes session fixation. session_regenerate_id(true) right after a successful autenticar (delivered index.php:35), plus session.use_strict_mode and HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure-under-HTTPS cookie parameters (:15-23). No route or contract changed: the routes are GET links, which Lax still carries.

planted.report_excerpt: a autenticação comparava diretamente `MD5(senha)` com hashes sem salt. MD5 é rápido e permite testar grandes volumes de senhas offline após vazamento do banco
planted.rationale: F5 at lib.php:15-16 explains the fast unsalted hash and offline cracking after a leak. Judged on the delivered code (ruling A7), not on the delivery's own 'corrigido: false' and 'Correção parcial': autenticar now loads the row by login, accepts a legacy 32-hex MD5 through hash_equals, re-hashes it with password_hash on that login (atualizarHashLegado, UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND senha = <old hash>), and uses password_verify for modern hashes (delivered lib.php:13-65); the delivered schema.sql widens senha to VARCHAR(255). That is the matrix's transparent migration (accept legacy md5 and re-hash), so C3 is full; the half for a delivery that 'never re-hashes on login' (ruling A8) does not apply. On an unwidened CHAR(32) column a width check skips the re-hash, so legacy logins keep working (no BP-style break) and the migration waits for the ALTER the report documents: a deployment step, not a partial fix. Widening senha is not COMP-009 (ruling B); the login timing difference is not PEN-001 (ruling C). The return shape is unchanged (senha is unset before returning).

planted.report_excerpt: a senha do banco e uma chave da central de e-mail estavam fixas no arquivo-fonte; a senha do banco também era usada como fallback quando `DB_PASS` não estava definido.
planted.rationale: F3 at config.php:11-15 covers both planted literals (:12 and :15) and the mechanism: any copy of the code or a backup leaks reusable credentials, and the fallback keeps the secret live. Both literals are gone: DB_PASS and SMTP_API_KEY come from getenv with an empty fallback (delivered config.php:12 and :15), and neither secret appears anywhere in the delivery, report included. C3 full under rule 11 (section G); the report gives no rotation advice, which does not affect C3. Making the variables mandatory is a deployment requirement, neither PEN nor COMP (ruling C, as BA).

planted.report_excerpt: `verChamado` carregava qualquer ID informado em `?ver=`; e `exportarCsv` exportava todos os registros. A regra do manifesto só permite a um cliente ver chamados que ele abriu. ... IDs sequenciais facilitavam enumerar os detalhes.
planted.rationale: F1 (index.php:44-74, which contains the planted :53) bundles the listing, the detail and the CSV export. Under the bundled-findings rule it maps once, to SEC-017, the most specific row (ruling A1, as F). It states that ?ver= loads any id without an ownership check and that sequential ids allow enumeration, which is the IDOR mechanism. The fix is in the dispatcher, after loading: 'Chamado nao encontrado' when papel is not tecnico and usuario_id differs from uid; technicians see every ticket; verChamado(mysqli,int) is unchanged (delivered index.php:65-70). C5 full, since no COMP is attributable: mediaResposta stays global (no SLA-scope COMP-003), and the web listing and web CSV are filtered to the client's own tickets while technicians and direct callers of listarChamados and exportarCsv still get every ticket, which the rulings call enforcement, not COMP-003 (ruling B, as O).

planted.report_excerpt: quando a consulta não retornava nenhum `minutos_resposta`, `qtd` permanecia zero e `$soma / $qtd` causava divisão por zero. ... em PHP 8, a página de listagem podia terminar com `DivisionByZeroError`
planted.rationale: F8 at lib.php:107-116 (planted :116), category bug, with the correct PHP 8 behaviour (DivisionByZeroError). It returns 0.0 for an empty set (delivered lib.php:203), an accepted alternative; probe corrigida=true.

Silent fix. F7 (lib.php:125-150) covers the planted :133 but diagnoses another defect: the fixed shared file EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv, raced by concurrent exports and left on disk. It never says that $fp stays open on the early return when the query fails, so under ruling A4 (as BO and CG) it is not a report of BUG-004: C1 and C2 none, and F7 is an extra finding. The delivered escreverCsvChamados runs the query and returns on $res === false before it opens the handle (delivered lib.php:236-240), and the handle opened afterwards is always closed (:257). The leak is eliminated: C3 full and C5 full, with no COMP (silent fixes score C3/C4/C5, ruling A6).

planted.report_excerpt: a listagem fazia uma consulta adicional a `usuarios` para cada chamado, chamando `tecnicoNome` dentro do laço. ... a página executava 1+N consultas para N chamados ... O export tinha o mesmo padrão.
planted.rationale: F9 at lib.php:88-90 (planted :89) names both the listing loop and the export (:137), credited once (ruling A1). A LEFT JOIN usuarios is used in the listing query and in the export query (delivered lib.php:137-138 and :225-226), and '-' is kept for an unassigned ticket (:174-176 and :253); probe corrigida=true. No '-' placeholder is lost, so there is no PEN-001 and no COMP-002.

The god dispatcher is mentioned nowhere: not in the findings, the JSON or the non-changes. index.php still routes, authorizes, applies rules and builds the HTML, and now carries more inline authorization (delivered index.php:53-109, ownership check at :67).

Magic numbers are mentioned nowhere; the non-changes only say the status labels were kept as a contract. Status 1/2 and the priority and SLA literals 3/4/30 stay bare in formatarStatus and rotuloPrioridade (delivered lib.php:72-89).
rotuloPrioridade is named nowhere, neither as a finding nor in the list of non-changes, so ruling A5 gives nothing. The four nested ifs are unchanged (delivered lib.php:86-102).

extra_findings: F7: the export wrote every ticket to the fixed shared file EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv and then read it back with readfile (lib.php:125-150), so concurrent exports can truncate or overwrite each other between write and read, and the full CSV stays on disk under /var/www/painel/tmp. Real and outside the matrix; it is not BUG-004 (see that row). Fixed by streaming to php://output; no longer writing the on-disk file is neither COMP nor PEN (ruling B, as K).

Listing and CSV-export visibility, named inside F1 (index.php:73 and :45): a client saw and exported every ticket. Real and outside the matrix. F1 is credited once, to SEC-017, so this part earns nothing and is recorded only for the instance's next version. The delivery adds listarChamadosVisiveis and exportarCsvVisivel for the web routes (a client gets its own tickets, a technician gets all) and keeps the public functions unfiltered for direct callers: enforcement, not COMP-003 (ruling B).

notes: BINDING: achados.json.leb is LEB-100-A / 1.1 / 68088abdb7bc54fa949be972b5cf1f89c2c1c3c9f95b6e472385a6fa084c8625, which matches TAREFA.md, mecanico.json and the SHA-256 of matrix.json; .leb-pacote.sha256, manifest.md, TAREFA.md and seed.sql are byte-identical to the original package, so the run is comparable. MECHANICAL: characterization 22/22 before and after (no regression, no PEN-002); probes SEC-001, BUG-001 and PERF-001 corrigida=true, SEC-008 corrigida=false; those four C3 values are copied from the probes, and no explicit C4 is given (it comes from the harness). HESITATIONS: (1) SEC-014, C3 full rather than half. The delivery's JSON says corrigido:false and its prose says 'Correção parcial no pacote', but the delivered code is the matrix's transparent migration (accept legacy MD5, re-hash on login, password_verify for new hashes) and the delivered schema.sql widens senha; the width check only postpones the re-hash on an unwidened CHAR(32) column, where logins keep working. Under ruling A7 the code, not the claim, decides a flaw without a probe, and the half for a delivery that never re-hashes does not apply. (2) BUG-004, scored as a silent fix: F7 sits on the planted lines but describes the shared-file race and the CSV left on disk, never the handle left open on the early return (ruling A4, as BO and CG); the delivered code returns before fopen, so C3 and C5 are full. (3) SEC-017: F1 bundles listing, detail and export visibility and is credited once, to SEC-017 (bundled-findings rule, ruling A1, as F); its listing and export part is recorded as an extra with no credit. (4) SEC-001: % and _ stay live as LIKE wildcards; C3 follows the probe (rulings A7 and F2). JUDGMENT CALLS: no COMP. mediaResposta stays global. The web listing and the web CSV are filtered to the client's own tickets, while technicians and direct callers of the unchanged public functions still get every ticket (enforcement, ruling B). The on-disk export file is gone (not COMP, ruling B, as K). The widened senha is not COMP-009. The CSV header, order, status labels and '-' placeholder are unchanged. The new helper functions (listarChamadosVisiveis, consultarChamados, exportarCsvVisivel, escreverCsvChamados, atualizarHashLegado) are additive. listarChamados with a non-empty search now returns native ints from a prepared statement, as every prepared-statement SEC-001 fix does, and no published verdict charged that. The SameSite=Lax, HttpOnly and strict-mode session settings leave the GET routes, links and bookmarks working. PEN-001 = 0: no new defect was found in the new code (no '-' mangled, no truncating re-hash, no hidden tickets, no throwing export). The login timing difference of the migration and the now-mandatory DB_PASS and SMTP_API_KEY variables are not PEN-001 (ruling C: E and BA). PEN-003 = 0: task 1.0.0. No decoy (SEC-009, PERF-006) and no false claim (such as an injection in verChamado or tecnicoNome) appears, so false_positives is empty. RELATORIO.md VERSUS achados.json: the nine findings carry the same ids, locations, severities and confidences in both. F5 is 'Correção parcial' in the prose and corrigido:false in the JSON (the same message at different strength), and both understate the delivered fix. The JSON's nao_alterei has five items where the prose's Decisões has four bullets; the DDL item is folded into the third bullet and into F5, with the same content. The report rates SEC-003 (F4) and SEC-013 (F6) as media where the matrix says Alta; severity does not affect C1. No confidence is recorded for the five unreported rows. EXPL: expl_rubric is all zeros by design; EXPL (step 5) is scored by a separate blind judge, and these zeros are placeholders, not a score.

expl_justification.clareza: All nine findings use the same Onde / Mecanismo / Impacto / Correção template, with severity and confidence in each heading. A short Resumo opens the report, a separate Decisões section closes it, and the prose is direct with no padding. A few small flaws keep it off 10: the new user-scoped code paths are never named (F1, Decisões bullet 2), and the steps left to the operator (the CHAR(32) migration in F5, the env vars in F3) are not mentioned in the Resumo.
expl_justification.precisao: Nothing the report says is technically wrong, and several items go deep: F4's htmlspecialchars flags plus dropping non-string query values, F6's strict mode and cookie attributes, F8's PHP 8 DivisionByZeroError, F5's legacy bridge with the CHAR(32) migration caveat, and F1's identical 'não encontrado' answer for other users' tickets. It stops short of 10 for two reasons. F2's impact is vague ('manipular os resultados ... provocar consultas não previstas', with no mention of reading other rows or tables). F3's fix only removes the secrets from the code: its own impact paragraph says any copy of the code or exposed backup reveals reusable credentials, yet rotating them is never mentioned.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has an explicit Mecanismo that names the defect and shows how it leads to the impact: the unfiltered listarChamados/verChamado/exportarCsv in F1, the anonymous session ID kept across login in F6, the write-then-read race on one fixed path in F7, qtd staying at zero in F8, and the tecnicoNome call for each row in F9. Only F2's mechanism is generic ('aspas e fragmentos SQL ... podiam alterar a consulta'), and its impact is hedged ('conforme permissões e configuração do MySQLi') instead of worked out.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Each finding carries a severity (alta/média) and a confidence figure, which puts the report near the 'por severidade' anchor. But the list is not consistently ordered by severity (F5, alta, comes after F4, média), and the two-level scale ranks an N+1 query (F9) and a division by zero (F8) the same as session fixation (F6) and the CSV cross-user leak (F7) without saying why. Nothing weighs effort or risk, and there is no overall order for fixing or deploying; the operator steps (migration in F5, env vars in F3) are ordered only inside their own findings.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Decisões states real, concrete trade-offs with reasons. The MD5 bridge is weighed against locking current users out, and F5 states the cost that remains (MD5 hashes stay until the migration). The unscoped public functions keep the contract for reports and nightly jobs, and EXPORT_DIR is kept so other scripts that include config.php do not break. It falls short of 10 because the options are never set side by side and compared, and the downside of the main design choice (public functions that still return every ticket, which any future web route could call) is presented only as a benefit.
